notes: v1.14.586 — ICON REFRESH. The installed-PWA identity becomes the chrome/neon ghost render, aligning the home-screen and tab icons with the shipped ghost boot screen. Spec docs/SHIP-HANDOFF-ICON-REFRESH.md (imported verbatim, sha256 81fc453fbcff47ce), Phase 0 census docs/ICON-REFRESH-PHASE0-EVIDENCE.md, owner GO on the mapping 2026-09-09 with one amendment (Q3). ACT: none of the three — identity/branding, not flow. DOOR LEDGER 0 opened / 0 closed; every tap count in the app is unchanged. ONE VISIBLE CHANGE: the app icon. WHAT SHIPPED: five files copied onto the five paths the code already referenced — apple-touch-icon.png (180x180), icon-192.png, icon-512.png, favicon-32.png, icon-512-maskable.png — so NO HTML and NO manifest path edit was needed for any of them (owner Q1: rename incoming onto existing paths). The only source edits besides the three stamps are two DELETIONS: the favicon-16 link in dct-ios.html and its manifest icons[] entry (owner Q2), because the incoming set has no 16 and the 32 covers every display that matters. favicon-16.png itself is LEFT ON DISK per spec section 4.1 — orphan cleanup is a follow-up ship, not this one. MEASURED, NOT TRUSTED: a PNG decoder (IHDR + inflate + unfilter, zlib only; there is no sharp on this box) read every pixel of all six PNGs. apple-touch-icon is colour type 2 with no alpha channel and four opaque corners — correct, because iOS composites transparency to black and an alpha'd apple-touch icon renders as a black square. icon-192/512 and favicon-32 are true alpha (54.6/56.0/43.0 percent transparent). THE MASKABLE IS THE OWNER'S AMENDMENT AND IT WAS RE-MEASURED: Q3 had recommended leaving the old opaque art because the new 512 is 56 percent transparent with fully transparent edges and would render as a shrunken ghost in an empty mask; the owner instead supplied a purpose-built icon-512-maskable.png and ruled that it ships. Verified before copying: 512x512, colour type 2 (opaque), background rgb(5,6,12) = #05060C, content bounding box 224x283 at (144,115)-(367,397), maximum content radius 152.1 px against the 204.8 px safe-zone requirement — it fits with 52.7 px of margin. Correct maskable art, so the manifest's purpose:maskable entry now carries the new identity too. WHY THE CACHE BUMP MATTERS HERE, corrected from the spec's assumption: none of the app icons is in PRECACHE_URLS and neither is manifest.json, but the fetch handler's same-origin branch is cache-first and cache.puts every successful GET under CACHE_VERSION — so an installed client holds the old icons in its runtime cache and would serve them indefinitely. The CACHE_VERSION bump is the ONLY thing that evicts them. NOT SHIPPED, all owner-ruled: phantom-ghost-256.webp (referenced by nothing, no target named — Q4) and phantom-icon-1024.png (master, 816 KB, referenced by nothing — Q5) stay out of the served root; icons/incoming/ deleted in this commit. UNTOUCHED AND UNEXAMINED BEYOND CONFIRMING THEY ARE NOT IN THE REFERENCE SET: the ghost boot sequence (phantom-ghost-v2/v3.webp), the nav icons (.tn-item .phantom-icon, the separate Grok-icon batch), the BUILD banner art, the OPS wall art. forge.html and index.html carry ZERO icon link tags and zero manifest link — measured, so forge is out of scope on evidence rather than assumption. ⚠ LEAD, NOT FIXED HERE, AND THE PHASE 0 CENSUS MISSED IT (it grepped served files, not tools/): tools/render-icons.js is the documented icon pipeline — its header reads 'Sources are the truth; PNGs are derived — re-run this, never hand-edit a PNG' — and it regenerates ALL SIX app icons from ghost.webp via sharp, including the favicon-16 this ship de-references and a maskable built with its own 410+51 padding math. ghost.webp is now stale art, and running that script would silently revert this entire ship. It cannot fire on the build box (no sharp installed) and nothing in the app calls it. The owner decides its disposition: retire the app-icon half, repoint it at the new master, or delete it. DEVICE CHECK is the spec's section 5 and its third item is the honest one: iOS bakes the home-screen icon at install time, so an already-installed PHANTOM keeps the old art until it is removed and re-added, which clears that install's data — the PHANTOM STAGING icon is the safer place to look.
